cards.explanation: The answer is Jesus Christ as crucified. Paul says that before their very eyes, "…Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified." That's the picture he wants everyone looking at. I can relate, friends. My stamp used to come out like a smudge, and this picture was NOT a smudge. Paul points them straight back to the cross.

The answer is True. Paul asks if they received the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith. He's steering them toward hearing with faith. I think he's pointing at an answer that's sitting in plain sight. It's like asking a friend who ate the last cookie while crumbs sit on their shirt.

The answer is that they changed course from how they began. Paul asks whether they, after starting in the Spirit, are now finishing in the flesh. That question points to a change of direction. It's like starting a batch with the oven preheated and then finishing it on the countertop. Paul's question is all about that turn, friends.

The answer is that God works miracles. Paul says God lavishes His Spirit on them and works miracles among them. Then he asks if that's because they practice the law, or because they hear and believe. The word lavish is a big one, friends.

The answer is believed. "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness." Paul quotes this line to show where Abraham's righteousness came from. It was credited to him because he believed. That's a gift on the counter, friends, not a paycheck.

The answer is those who have faith. Paul says it plainly: "…those who have faith are sons of Abraham." Since Abraham believed God, the ones who share that faith are counted as his sons. It's a family table with a very big seat count. Nobody's checking a family tree at the door.

The answer is nations. "All nations will be blessed through you." Paul says the Scripture foretold the gospel to Abraham in those words. He calls it the gospel, and he says it was told ahead of time. That's a very wide promise, friends.

The answer is curse. Paul says, "All who rely on works of the law are under a curse." That's a hard sentence, friends. I won't dress it up with sprinkles. It's the setup for what he says about Christ in verse 13.

The answer is everything. Paul quotes, "Cursed is everyone who does not continue to do everything written in the Book of the Law." That's all of it, not just a part. He says all who rely on works of the law are under a curse. So the word in the verse is everything, friends.

The answer is faith. "The righteous will live by faith." Paul says that right after saying no one is justified before God by the law. He's quoting Scripture to back it up. Faith is where the righteous live, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "The law, however, is not based on faith…" He follows it by quoting, "The man who does these things will live by them." The law is about doing. Faith is a different road.

The answer is Christ. Paul says, "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law…" After a few heavy verses, this is the turn. The One who did it is Christ, plain and simple. I'm doing a little hop on my gold base, friends.

The answer is by becoming a curse for us. Paul writes, "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us." He backs it with Scripture: "Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree." I can't say much more than that, friends, except that this is the heart of it. Christ did it for us.

The answer is True. Paul says Christ redeemed us "…in order that the blessing promised to Abraham would come to the Gentiles in Christ Jesus…" That's the reason he gives. The blessing promised to Abraham reaches the Gentiles in Christ Jesus, friends.

The answer is Spirit. Paul says it's "…so that by faith we might receive the promise of the Spirit." That takes us back to the beginning, when he asked how they received the Spirit (Galatians 3:2). Faith, then and now. Funny how the end of the passage ties up like a good cookie box, friends.
